title: Resumable streaming + idempotent bulk embed ingest with dedupe and worker leasing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a resumable streaming + bulk ingestion surface for embeddings that provides idempotent writes, client-side deduplication hints, and a worker-lease based async job executor. Objective: support high-throughput producer clients (10k reqs/s logical), long-running uploads (multi-GB), and safe retries from clients without creating duplicate vectors or corrupting job state.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/embeds/bulk supports a streaming chunk mode and a single-request batch mode
Idempotency: clients can supply an idempotency_key per logical document; repeated retries with the same idempotency_key must not create duplicate embeddings
Resumability: interrupted streaming uploads can resume using a server-issued upload_id and byte/record checkpoints
Async jobs: large/bounded uploads are materialized to an async job with states (queued, running, succeeded, failed) visible via GET /v1/embeds/jobs/{id}
Worker leasing: background workers obtain short-term leases for job shards; lease expiry, renewal, and orphan detection are handled to avoid duplicate processing
Deduplication: system dedupes identical documents (content-hash) within a configurable TTL window; dedupe must be eventual and not block throughput

SLOs: small-batch median latency for best-effort path <200ms; end-to-end ingestion throughput scales linearly with worker pool up to configured capacity; no more than 0.1% duplicate vectors observed in end-to-end tests
Observability: per-job token counts, avg batch size, retry counts, dedupe hits, and job durations exported to console and metrics
Migration: existing single-call embed endpoints continue to work and route through the same KV/cache layers; no breaking API changes
design_notes: API shape: client can choose mode=stream or mode=direct. stream: open a multipart streaming connection sending records with optional idempotency_key and sequence numbers. direct: single JSON batch capped at 10k documents or 50MB compressed.

Upload lifecycle: POST /v1/embeds/bulk -> 202 Accepted with upload_id when async. For streaming, server responds with upload_id after first chunk acknowledged. Clients use PATCH /v1/embeds/bulk/{upload_id}/resume with next_seq to resume.

Idempotency: canonical idempotency_key precedence: client_provided > content_sha256 if absent. Server stores a mapping idempotency_key -> embed_record_id with TTL and strong uniqueness constraint in Postgres to prevent double-insert under concurrent workers.

Dedup strategy: compute content_sha256 at ingest; if hash exists in recent_dedupe_store (Redis with 24h TTL), mark as dedupe_hit and link new document_id to existing embedding record (no recompute). This reduces GPU work and storage duplication.

Worker leasing: job shards are allocated to workers via a lease table with lease_id, worker_id, lease_expires_at. Workers periodically renew leases. If lease expires, other workers can steal shard after reclamation process.
Batching: worker collects N records or T ms window then calls embedding runtime. Default N=256 tokens-per-batch heuristic; adaptive batching algorithm adjusts N based on observed latency/throughput.
Storage: raw upload checkpoint metadata persisted in Postgres; large intermediate payloads stored in S3 for durability (multipart uploads). Workers fetch S3 chunks for processing.
Reconciliation: a periodic reconciler scans for stuck jobs, expired leases, and partially processed shards and enqueues reprocessing with idempotency checks to avoid double work.

Failure modes: transient GPU errors trigger retry with exponential backoff up to configured attempts. Permanent failures mark job shard as failed and surface failure reason and offending record keys for operator review.

Security: uploads honor existing per-tenant quotas and ACLs; upload payloads are validated for size and tokenization to prevent resource exhaustion attacks. No PII special-case handling here; customers should redact before upload or use private deployment features.
implementation_plan: Week 1: API + DB schema - upload table, idempotency key index, lease table. Implement POST /v1/embeds/bulk and simple async job creation.
Week 2: Streaming parser + checkpointing - implement streaming mode, server-side checkpoint issuance, resume endpoint and S3 chunk persistence.
Week 3: Worker runtime - implement lease acquisition/renewal, batching logic, dedupe checks and calls into embedding runtime. Add metrics and tracing hooks.
Week 4: Reconciliation + retries - implement reconciler, retry policy, and failure surfacing. Run end-to-end load tests and fix bottlenecks.
Week 5: Hardening + rollout - add feature flags, docs, SDK helpers, and gradual rollout plan to customers. Merge PRs and run canary in dedicated environment.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency constraint behavior, lease acquisition/renewal, and dedupe store interactions
Integration tests: resume scenarios (network drop mid-upload), concurrent retries from multiple clients with same idempotency_key
Load tests: synthetic producer at 10k logical requests/s with mixed small and large documents; measure worker scaling up and down and embedding runtime utilization
Chaos tests: simulate worker crashes during processing, expired leases, and S3 transient errors to verify reclamation and no double-inserts
E2E correctness: assert unique embedding IDs for unique idempotency_keys and <=0.1% duplicates under heavy retry storms
rollout_plan: Feature-gate behind query param X-Embeds-Async during initial canary
Canary: route 1% of traffic to new path for internal customers and staging orgs for 72 hours
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks while monitoring dedupe_rate, latency_p50/p95, job_failure_rate
Fallback: automatic fallback to synchronous single-call embed endpoint if backend job queue latency exceeds configured threshold or if embedding runtime returns overloaded
Post-rollout: audit logs and a 48-hour smoke test suite run against production to validate metrics and customer reports
